claims.text: In situ aberration-corrected TEM with a heating stage can directly reveal atomic-scale structural dynamics and phase behavior during high-temperature exposure.
The AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles are nearly equiatomic.
The as-synthesized AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles form a single-phase nanoalloy.
The as-synthesized AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles have a homogeneous atomic distribution.
An integrated TEM heating stage can be used to heat a sample in situ.
Heating in the TEM can reproduce controlled high-temperature service conditions.
The experiment can maintain the nanoparticles in vacuum while keeping electron-beam damage minimal.
Heating may produce defect evolution, phase-boundary migration, or nanoparticle coarsening.
Thermal energy drives atomic motion, phase transitions, and defect migration.
Real-time observation of atomic dynamics can test predicted enhanced thermal stability attributed to thermodynamic contributions.
Elevated temperature may cause observable changes in lattice spacing or defect structures, or may leave the structure stable.
The as-synthesized baseline has no high-temperature-induced structural degradation.
Electron-beam effects and sample-thickness constraints may limit interpretation of the in situ TEM results.
Intrinsic thermal behavior must be distinguished from electron-beam-induced imaging artifacts.
Atomic-resolution TEM images can be continuously recorded while temperature is increased.
Lattice spacings, grain-boundary dynamics, phase changes, defects, and nanoparticle morphology can be monitored as functions of temperature.
Absence of significant atomic-scale changes at elevated temperature would falsify the proposed method's ability to reveal intrinsic high-temperature structural dynamics.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and predicted outcome treat structural stability with no rearrangement as a valid observable result, but the falsification rule says that observing no significant atomic-scale changes would falsify the hypothesis. No change could instead be evidence of thermal stability, so it is not by itself a decisive falsifier of the method.
